prompt:
It became a running joke,
Could I ever write down what we just said?
The truth flares bright between us,
Then vanishes, baby, vanishes instead.

Rule number one — I scrawl in ink:
Don’t start from what you’re not.
Blueprints for a better me?
Tried it. Failed. Forgot.

[Chorus - Guitars open full strum · Tambourine on 2 & 4 · Bass slides into each chord.]
This is my evil plan — yeah!
Grow tomatoes, in the frying pan,
Be the Lizard King if I damn well can.
Not just normal, baby, I wanna be grand.
Sing poems at the dive bar, write checks I can’t cash,
Do yoga, drink whiskey, make a mad dash.

[Verse — slightly off kilter sudden tempo shift, “Warm Gun” mode]
He said he was the Lizard King…
Well, me too, I swing like a pendulum thing.
He called me Lizard Queen, I laughed 
Then lost myself inside a draft. (Draft of what? Doesn’t matter)
The garden grows its crooked green,
Tomatoes traded for a dream.
And those who plant a ragged row
Are taught by neighbors how to grow.

[Bridge -gentle, “Dear Prudence” style lift]
The sublime and the stupid — side by side.
A burlesque of truth I no longer hide.
I don’t want safe. I want fun.
I want to strip down laughing in the midday sun.
Wear the crazy thing like it's my skin
Pretend it’s my first time again.

[Chorus 2 – Rising tempo]
This is my evil plan! 
Grow zucchinis in a coffee can,
Channel ghosts from a soda stand,
Be Beer Garden royalty, bare feet in the sand.
Write epiphanies in traffic, burn bridges with flair,
Treat strangers like friends — pretend I care.

[Refrain – Spoken call and response]
What happens?
(What happens?)
What happens when I stop pretending?
(Stop pretending!)
What happens when the beat keeps lending
Me a life I can dance in,
A life I can end in.

[Final Chorus - full harmony bloom]
This is my evil plan — to grow what I can,
In a beer-garden town with a notebook in hand.
Don’t want to be a brand, don’t want to be bland,
Let me be strange — this is my evil plan.
Not perfect, not polished, just real as I am,
Let me be messy, let me be grand,
Let me begin — this is my evil plan.

[Outro – Whisper / Shout cycle]
Stand up straight.
That’s the start.
That’s the whole damn plan.
(yeah… yeah…)
Stand up straight.
That’s the start.
That’s the whole damn plan.
[fade out on organ swirl and heartbeat drum]

prompt:
SEVENTEEN AGAIN

I lost my job like a house key
Somewhere between Tuesday and pride
Woke up at ten with the sun in my teeth
And a stranger where the schedule used to hide
The coffee tasted like a dare
The mirror looked underage
I put on a hoodie I don’t remember buying
And stepped out of my proper age

The bills got loud, the days got loose
My backbone turned to bubblegum
I heard the clock say “do what you want”
In the voice of someone dumb and young

I went seventeen again
Cheap soda, big emotions
Seventeen again
Bad plans and perfect notions
I’m eating cereal like it’s dinner with a friend
Yeah life got loud and thin
And I went seventeen again

I made a playlist like a manifesto
Songs to testify in court
Told my reflection “you’re a problem child”
She said, “baby, file a report”
The fridge sang hymns at midnight
The couch became my throne
I googled “careers for former adults”
And how to not die alone

Responsibility wore soft shoes
Snuck out the back while I slept
Left a note that said “grow up soon”
I said, “sure,” and overslept

I went seventeen again
Eyeliner like a battle plan
Seventeen again
Falling for the pizza man
Every feeling turned up to ten
Like the world just learned my name
Yeah I went seventeen again

She lives in my ribcage, feral and bored
Knows every dumb song I adored
She drives with the seat too far back
Laughs at the maps I hoard
Says, “Relax, the future’s a rumor
The past is a bad cover band”
Hands me a lighter, says “try this life on”
Like it’s a jacket from a friend

Seventeen again
With pockets full of nothing
Seventeen again
Brave about the wrong things

Seventeen again
But older in the knees
Seventeen again
Apologizing to my keys
I’ll let her drive around the bend
Till the grown-up lights come on
Yeah I went seventeen again
And somehow I’m not gone

The adult keeps knocking
With a résumé and shoes
But the kid’s got the stereo 
And she likes to choose.

prompt:
Junkyard for the Soul’s Discontent

[Verse 1]
I lost a piece of me in the rain last night,
Heard it land without a sound.
Just a flicker slipping out of sight,
Too small for anyone to notice falling down.

Where do the broken fragments drift—
The ones too quiet to retrieve?
Do they ride the backs of passing winds
Or cling to things that never leave?

[Pre-Chorus]
I wonder if they gather somewhere unseen,
Behind the hours we never kept—
A field of everything we almost were,
And everything we quietly left.

[Chorus]
Are my missing socks guiding lost parts of me,
Wearing thin through the floor of eternity?
Every thread undone, every promise spent—
Where’s the junkyard for the soul’s discontent?

Do they hum with the lives I never tried,
Stacked like shoes no one would buy?
Every small goodbye, every accident—
Where’s the junkyard for the soul’s discontent?

[Verse 2]
Is there a corner where the liars sit,
Hands folded like they’re still believed?
A heap of truths we never said aloud,
Still warm from being concealed?

Is there a shelf of unlived afternoons,
Still smelling faintly of sun and dust?
A box of laughter sealed too soon
Because we thought it wasn’t enough?

[Pre-Chorus]
I wonder if they gather there in rows,
The lives we never dared to keep—
Breathing softly in the dark,
Waiting for us in our sleep.

[Chorus]
Are my missing socks guiding lost parts of me,
Walking slow through infinity?
Every fracture kept, every moment bent—
Where’s the junkyard for the soul’s discontent?

Do they wait where forgotten things reside,
With the selves we set aside?
Every version lost, every accident—
Where’s the junkyard for the soul’s discontent?

[Outro — quiet, unresolved]
If I went looking, would I recognize
What I left behind?
Or would it recognize me first?

prompt:
Monsters You Don’t See

I trusted myself.

That was the deal.

I trusted myself to survive myself.
To invest everything—time, energy, sanity—into whatever future I believed in.
To take risks, knowing I would be there to catch the fall.

Or at least, that’s what I told myself.

If I’m honest, the only promise I’ve ever truly kept was simpler than survival.

I promised myself an interesting life.

And I’ve kept that promise.

At any cost.

When I worked as a case manager, I saw it happen all the time.
One missed paycheck became two.
One disruption became collapse.

Once the structure cracks, gravity finishes the job.

But when it happened to me, it didn’t feel like collapse.

It felt like confusion.

Like I’d stepped slightly out of sync with reality—
and everyone else could still hear the music.

I had savings.
Credentials.
Evidence of competence.

I assumed the interruption would be temporary.

That was two years ago.

Since then, I’ve performed competence like theater.

Interviews where I faltered.
Interviews where I was flawless.

One recruiter said I crushed it.
Said no one else had gone above and beyond the way I had.

I believed her.

Nothing happened.

Again and again: enthusiasm, validation, silence.

Not rejection. Not failure.

Erasure.

I started to wonder if there was something on me.

Not visible.
But detectable.

Something that made systems recoil.

Something without a name.

In a way, I succeeded.

I gave myself exactly what I promised.

An interesting life.

I took the risk.
I let myself believe in my own autonomy.

I relaxed.

I trusted the version of me that had always survived before.

What followed wasn’t rest.

It was annihilation.

Not physical.

Emotional annihilation.

The slow disintegration of certainty.

I didn’t fight it.

I lay down.

And for a while, I stayed there.

That’s when I met the monsters.

Not under the bed.

Inside possibility.

They weren’t creatures.
They were versions.

Possible lives.
Possible endings.

Each one waiting patiently for permission.

Monsters aren’t what you think.

They aren’t evil.

They’re just futures that haven’t been chosen yet.

If you see one clearly—really see it—it isn’t hunting you.

It’s lost.

It’s waiting to see what you’ll become.

It’s the monsters you don’t see that matter.

The ones that never announce themselves.

The ones already living in your blind spots.

They don’t need fear.

They don’t need permission.

They already know something you don’t.

They know you are capable of becoming them.

Maybe that’s what this is.

Not failure.

Not misalignment.

Transformation without instructions.

A life that doesn’t resolve cleanly.

A story that refuses employability as its final form.

Maybe this is what it costs to keep your promise.

To choose experience over stability.

To choose uncertainty over obedience.

To choose yourself—
without knowing what that self will become.

I wanted an interesting life.

I got one.

Now I just have to survive it.

One disruption became collapse.

Once the structure cracks, gravity finishes the job.

It felt like confusion.

Like I’d stepped slightly out of sync with reality—
and everyone else could still hear the music.

I had savings.

Evidence of competence.

I assumed the interruption would be temporary.

That was two years ago.

Since then, I’ve performed competence like theater.

Interviews where I was flawless.

One recruiter said I crushed it.
Said no one else had gone above and beyond the way I had.

I believed her.

Nothing happened.

Not rejection. Not failure.

Erasure.

I started to wonder if there was something on me.

Not visible.
But detectable.

Something that made systems recoil.

Something without a name.

I gave myself exactly what I promised.

I took the risk.
I let myself believe in my own autonomy.

I relaxed.

It was annihilation.

Emotional annihilation.

I lay down.

Not under the bed.

Inside possibility.

They were versions.

Possible lives.
Possible endings.

It’s lost.

They don’t need permission.

Not misalignment.

Transformation without instructions.

A life that doesn’t resolve cleanly.

A story that refuses employability as its final form.

Maybe this is what it costs to keep your promise.

To choose experience over stability.

To choose uncertainty over obedience.

To choose yourself—
without knowing what that self will become.

I got one.

Now I just have to survive it.

prompt:
[Soft analog synth pad: low, almost HVAC-like]
[Muted piano: sparse, single-note pulses]
[Electronic percussion: distant, filtered clicks]
[Sub bass drone: slow, steady, almost imperceptible]
[Field recording: faint office ambience, fluorescent buzz]
[Nylon-string: close, dry, human. Fingers audible.]
[Bass: steady pulse, slightly ahead.]
[Electric: low-gain, muted tension under everything.]

Verse 1

They don’t break you anymore.
They streamline you.

Sand the edges off your hours,
Shave the marrow from your days.
You wake up owing someone something
Before your feet hit the floor.

A password, a code, a second attempt—
Prove you’re you once more.

Verse 2

Every doorway has a funnel now,
Every errand has a queue.
You gather screenshots like receipts
For battles you never chose to pursue.

The help desk hums in canned replies,
Warmth outsourced overseas.
You learn to say “I understand”
While kneeling to the fees.

Chorus

We call it access.
Call it progress.
Call it just how things evolve.

But every day feels fractional—
A thousand cuts you can’t resolve.

The war inside isn’t thunder.
It’s small and itemized.
Heaven and hell don’t argue anymore—
[almost whisper] They’re quietly monetized.

Verse 3

Your data floats in distant air,
Your labor feeds a graph.
Your rest becomes a productivity tip,
Your grief a trending draft.

Even mistakes aren’t human now—
They auto-post and stick.
Forty-two points fall overnight
On a system built too quick.

Bridge

What if exhaustion isn’t weakness
But proof of something drained?
What if the flaw’s not in your habits
But in a world designed for gain?

What if the holy thing is saying,
“I’m not a resource to refine”?
What if the sin is calling this
A fair and neutral time?

Chorus

We call it freedom.
Call it choice.
Call it “just participate.”

But every click is shaving something
From the person we create.

The war inside is subtle—
It doesn’t scream or stall.
Heaven and hell share the same dashboard now,
And they’re extracting it all.

Final Verse (soft)

It’s not collapse.
It’s erosion.

It’s Tuesday in fluorescent light.
It’s fighting to be recognized
By systems that forgot your name.

Heaven and hell aren’t myths anymore.
They’re margins on a sheet.
And every morning you wake up
Already slightly incomplete.

[Last line barely above a whisper. Nylon sustains unresolved. Bass drops. Long silence.]

I renamed the ache agenda,
Ironed it flat, folded it neat.
Pinned a scent of citrus to the bruise
So no one smelled the bleed.

Smiled while it settled clean.
Called the hush a power move
When it was fear dressed up as lean.

Verse 2

I’ve shared a bed with my better judgment,
Felt it turning toward the wall.
Heaven wasn’t light breaking open—
It was me not answering the call.

Hell was never brimstone loud.
It was yes in softer tones.

Signed in careful pen strokes.

Anoint it as design.

Call it timing, call it fine.

The war inside looks courteous.
It smiles and pours the wine.
While heaven and hell split custody
Of a life that’s meant to be mine.

Verse 3

The devil speaks in my cadence
When I’m weary of the climb.
God is the draft I almost send
But delete for being “too much” this time.

I’ve asked for maps to places
My hands already knew.
Built altars out of tolerance
While the exits glowed in view.

Bridge

What if the crime was not exploding,
But shrinking by degree?
What if the prize for staying quiet
Was just a version less like me?

What if all this calm composure
Wasn’t noble, wasn’t right?
Just the practiced art of freezing
When I should have picked the fight?

Chorus
We canonize the compromise,
An alibi we use.
We bless what blunts and hollows us
So we don’t have to choose.

But the war inside is civil—
No sirens, no display.
Just heaven and hell under one thin sheet
With the vows we’re scared to break.

It isn’t thunder.
It’s subtraction.
It’s choosing not to choose.

And tying smaller shoes.

They live inside your skin.
Morning comes without a verdict.
You rise.
You do what you did.

[Intro] Is this thing still free speech? Or did that get sold in the lobby too?

Hey Mr. President—what the fuck is wrong with you? You sold the shirts, named the rooms, and minted the myth, But you’re holding a sword with nothing to hit. Somewhere between Tuesday and pride

I put on a hoodie I don’t remember buying

My backbone turned to bubblegum
I heard the clock say “do what you want”
In the voice of someone dumb and young

I went seventeen again
Cheap soda, big emotions
Seventeen again
Bad plans and perfect notions

Yeah life got loud and thin

The fridge sang hymns at midnight
The couch became my throne
I googled “careers for former adults”
And how to not die alone

Snuck out the back while I slept
Left a note that said “grow up soon”
I said, “sure,” and overslept

I went seventeen again
Eyeliner like a battle plan
Seventeen again
Falling for the pizza man
Every feeling turned up to ten
Like the world just learned my name
Yeah I went seventeen again

With pockets full of nothing
Seventeen again

But older in the knees
Seventeen again
Apologizing to my keys

With a résumé and shoes
But the kid’s got the stereo

Title: Connection Lost (Participant Observer) Vibe: Industrial 

(Verse 1) Pack the bags, I was two and a half The accident tore the map in half Grandma’s porch, then back to Mom Bionic leg, just keeping calm Found a safe place, for a year or two But the floor falls out, yeah it always do I was six, I was eight, doing the math Participant observer on a winding path.

(Pre-Chorus) And every house had a different rule Every kitchen was a different school "What is this now?" I asked the room Trying to decode the tune I didn't get scared, I didn't freeze. I learned to love the changing breeze.

(Chorus) Connection lost, download failed The anchor lifted, the ship just sailed Too slippery to catch, too fast to mold I missed the warmth, but I missed the cold The system tried to log me in But I was gone before the code could begin I don't want the box, I don't want the design I’m running on a custom line.

(Verse 2) I never needed a TV screen To watch the adults do the same routine The cool one, the sad one, the one with the glare I dissected them all from the living room chair A different mask on every face A different script in every place I shut my eyes to disappear And found a god inside my ear.

(Bridge) (Tempo slows, heavy tension) Now the house is quiet, the house is still And I’m looking for the void to fill Safe is boring, safe is a lie I need the thunder to know I’m alive I make the move that looks insane And find the logic in the rain.

(Guitar Solo) (Chaotic, noisy, triumphant)

(Verse 3 / Breakdown) Now my son asks, "Mom, what’s our tradition?" I look at him blank, like a lost transmission I don't have rituals from the past I built a life that wasn't built to last We start from scratch, we start from zero No family curse, no family hero.

(Outro) They call me weird, they say I’m strange I’m only happy when it starts to change. Interrupted signal. Interrupted lies. I watch the crash with my own two eyes. Connection lost... Connection saved.

using the chair to hold my nouns.

could move the words back inside?

Change where you sit,

Every good idea needs better conditions,

call it posture, call it rebellion, call it fate.
Turns out inspiration’s just ergonomics
with a little less shame and a better angle on the day.

Don’t tempt me I might stay awhile.
I could live on this porch forever,
cement block throne, weatherproof style.

something sacred, something bold,

then this is where I’m getting old.

or start judging my résumé
this is a controlled experiment,
and yes, it’s Jimmy Buffett at two pee em

with a lack of intent.
I’m very serious about this nonsense
every word’s well meant.

tags: cute female vocal, cutecore,  punchy bass, dynamic flow, dynamic drops, fast flow,, bright synths, smooth flow, bedroom pop, miami bass, idol, moé voice, complex, trip
prompt:
Oh billionaires, bless your tiny hearts,
must be hard owning everything and calling it a fair start.
You got twelve yachts, three rockets, and a private moon hotel,
but somehow every tax bill seems to ring your personal bell.

You lay off half the country just to give your stock a kiss,
then tweet some hustle porn about success is not a myth.
You buy another mansion when emotions get intense…
because nothing screams trauma like “I bought the Parthenon for cents.”

Aw, poor baby billionaire,
is your gold too heavy to bear?
Does the butler forget your favorite chair?
Do you cry in your caviar? 

Billionaires, bless their tiny hearts,
how do they spend so many days tearing dreams apart?
They hoard the world then call it God’s reward,
and say the poor just need to work a little more.

Billionaires, bless their tiny hearts,
building bunkers just in case the peasants learn to start
asking questions like “Hey, who made the rules?”
and “Why’s the world run by the richest fools?”

Oh billionaires, we really understand,
it’s hard to pick a favorite Gulfstream when you never land.
You got a superyacht submarine and a helipad on board 
but teachers gotta fund their classrooms at the goddamn Dollar Store.

You get a tax break every time you exhale,
and if you murder a pension fund you get a bonus in the mail.
You call the workers family until the numbers trend 
and suddenly your family meets the exit sign again.

Poor baby billionaire,
does compassion thin out in the air
halfway up the billionaire stair?

Billionaires, bless their tiny hearts,
their empathy’s so small it needs museum parts.
Guess money doesn’t buy a soul or conscience,
just 47 lawmakers on retainer for responses.

Billionaires, bless their tiny hearts,
crying “innovation” while they strip the world apart.
If greed was a religion they’d be saints of Mars,
burning every ladder that got them to the stars.

You can be anything you dream…
please ignore the giant guillotine.

“Work hard! Grind harder! Don’t sleep! Don’t eat!”
Oh wait, that’s only for the folks you beat.
You built an empire on exhausted backs
then wrote a TED Talk telling us we just lack hacks.

Billionaires, bless their tiny hearts,
they preach charity while they buy spare body parts.
They say “we’re all equal” from the Coral Reef Wing 
while the rest of us pray the rent fairy swings.

Billionaires, bless their tiny hearts,
if the world collapses they’ll retreat to space bazaars.
But one thing money can’t protect you from:
a planet full of people who finally wake up.

Sleep tight, money kings.

prompt:
It’s been one week since I quit my job,
five days since I blamed the fog,
three days since I texted back 
and pretended that I didn’t, but I did, in fact.
Yesterday, I tried to manifest,
but the Wi-Fi’s down and I failed the test.
You laughed at me, I laughed at you 
we’re both just ghosts with rent past due.

Hold it now and watch the tape,
it’s me at three a.m. eatin’ frosted grapes,
while arguing with my reflection’s face 
“you’re fine!” “you’re not!” “you need more space.”

The Smoking Man’s in this one 
snuck in my dream with a Payless coupon,
offered me truth for a discount fee,
said “The X-Files lied but not to me.”
Yeah, The Smoking Man’s in this one,
chain-smokin’ logic in aisle three,
If you see him, tell him I’m on the run 
from normalcy and my old ID.

made art with grief and folding chairs,
one week since I painted kids room 
and turned trauma into peach cartoon.
I’m thinkin’ maybe I should meditate,
but I’d rather caffeinate and pontificate,
can’t ghost myself, I’ve tried before 
kept sending me memes from 2004.

Stop, collaborate, and disassociate,
I can overthink faster than you can hate.
I’m a walking self-help paperback 
highlighted wrong and never gave it back.

The Smoking Man’s in this one 
left me a note in the checkout lane,
“Trust no man who explains your pain,”
so I blocked him then wrote this refrain.
Yeah, The Smoking Man’s in this one,
he’s narrating my existential spin,
said “you can’t out-weird your fate, my friend,”
I said, “watch me hit record again.”

painted walls while the voices knit,
a scarf of shame that don’t quite fit.

I got art supplies and daddy issues,
burned my resume, grew tattoos,
now the HR file’s just bad reviews.

The Smoking Man’s in this one,
sells paranoia by the carton, hon,
he winked and said, “It’s all been spun,”
and I laughed because I am the pun.
Yeah, The Smoking Man’s in this one,
chain-smokin’ doubt and metaphors,
I’m fine, I’m free, I’m slightly done 
but I’ll be back for the encore.

prompt:
Our conversation got me thinking about many things, of course.
You said something small, almost offhand, but it lodged itself in my mind. It didn’t even relate directly to what we were talking about this morning, but it opened a door.
So I’m stepping through it.
This is about one of the curses I struggle with.
When I hear people say they’re going to move in together, I cringe. People have all sorts of reasons many of which used to be my own.
“Well, we’re always spending the night at his place anyway.”
 “It’s stupid to pay for two apartments. Think of what we could do with the extra money.”
To this I say: spend the money and save your soul.
Harsh, maybe but for me, imperative.
It’s about control.
When I live with someone, I start to become someone else. It’s the downside of being a good chameleon.
In its mild form, it’s like taking a two-week trip through Kentucky and coming back with a flawless Southern accent that takes months to lose. I become where I am, or who I’m with.
In its worst form, it’s terrifying.
 Because if the environment turns negative, I turn with it. I start mirroring shadows, absorbing moods that aren’t mine.
That’s why control of my environment is non-negotiable.
 I can’t share this space—not the one that keeps me from dissolving.
 This is the sacred space that prevents me from becoming someone else entirely.
The answer seems easy, and in a way, it is.
 I even wrote a piece once titled “Don’t Move In.”
So yes, the solution is simple. But it’s also painful.
It’s not that I don’t want to share a home and life with a partner.
 It’s that I’m unable to.
Every time I’ve tried, I’ve failed.
And as I write this, I think I’m having a small breakdown not dramatic, just honest. I’m crying, and that’s okay.
I’m mourning the loss of something I still desire.
Why wouldn’t I want that?
 Why shouldn’t I?




I can’t remember the last person who made my knees weak.
And here’s the conclusion I’ve come to
I’ve never been bitten with such finesse.

That line above, about consent, control, precision
rings truer than most philosophy I’ve read.
The ear bite proved it.
Anyone else? It’d be comic. Or catastrophic.

You once said, “All my shit comes from childhood.”
You never said what shit.

We talked about focus.
You asked if I could stay with something boring.
I probably said yes.
The truth is no.
I skim life until it feels complete.

I tell myself
he’s just a good distraction.
But when have I ever recognized a bad one?

When we’re face-to-face, I’m all in.
I don’t stop to document,
I stay until the moment burns through.
Later, I write it
once it’s ripened into meaning.

If you want, I’ll read it aloud next time.
Or send it. Or both.

Control?
I wouldn’t say I need all of it.
I’m not obsessed.
I’m a minimalist control freak.

Mostly, I control myself.
Topping myself is exhausting
but it’s what saved me.

Handing it over to anyone else?
Would’ve been a disaster.

Hopefully, you don’t want to mutilate me
any more than I want to be mutilated.

Growing up, everyone around me
made bad decisions for me
or good ones for themselves.

So I learned early:
no one’s coming to save me.
I dreamed of turning eighteen.
Finally, I’d decide.
And I did.

Daddy issues?
Absolutely.
Obviousfuckingly so.

Do I want him to do this to me?
Yes.
And just imagining it
makes my skin flush
like it might melt off my bones.

I think about my father’s advice.
I needed to believe he loved me enough to play me
to use what he knew about me
for my own good.

His truest message was this:

“Kid, don’t forget this country was built by rebels.
And you’re a rebel.”

Every little girl wants to believe her father knows her.

I read an essay
“Authority, Submission, and Freedom.”
And thought
Well, shit. That explains a lot.

I love taking direction.
Crave it.
But not from just anyone.

Give me direction that serves me
and I’ll give you everything I have.
No hesitation.
No shame.
Just recognition.
Acceptance.
A small rebellion against denial.

Thank you.

My father used to say
“Men just want to fuck you.
Women need to know how to cook.”

Somehow, I agreed.
And also took it as a dare.

Maybe he said it knowing
I’d spend my life proving him wrong.
Maybe I keep seeking men
who’ll point me the wrong way
just to prove
I can still find my own.

It’s all good, girl.
You’re still the rebel
Daddy told you to be.

prompt:
Monsters You Don’t See
I was able to take a chance on myself invest in myself because I trusted myself to do what needed to be done to take care of myself.
 Or at least, that’s what I told myself.
Of course I’ll take a short-term risk and invest everything I have into an idea my time, energy, sanity if I think it’ll be worth it. I’ve always believed I could trust myself to take care of myself.
Or did I?
If I’m honest, the only promise I’ve ever truly kept to myself is this: I will ensure an interesting experience.
As a case manager at the employment office, I used to see it all the time once one thing slips, everything slips, especially if that thing is your job. But when my job slipped (if you can even call it that it was more like getting my hopes up sky-high before watching them crushed to dust), I didn’t feel it all at once.
At first, I was just shocked. Baffled. I felt stupid and crazy, like I’d missed something everyone else could see. Still, I had savings, a little cushion, and enough faith in my skills, work ethic, and education to assume I’d bounce back quickly.
That was two years ago.
Since then, I’ve had interviews where I stumbled, and others where I killed it. One recruiter even told me I “crushed it.” The hiring team had been thrilled by my pre-interview work apparently, no one else had gone “above and beyond” the way I had. Surely, this would go well.
It didn’t.
Same story, over and over promising start, strong interview, radio silence. By the third time, I started to wonder if I was cursed. Like there was something on me that I couldn’t scrub off, something invisible repelling opportunity. I asked for feedback. Nothing. Ghosted, again and again.
So, in a way, I’ve succeeded. I did give myself the “interesting experience” I promised. I took a chance on me, let myself relax, believed I could do whatever I wanted. Why shouldn’t I? I’d worked hard, earned the credentials, avoided disaster wasn’t this supposed to be the reward?
But what followed wasn’t rest. It was annihilation.
 Emotional annihilation.
I was wrecked but I didn’t want to get up. So I didn’t. I lay down. And for a while, I enjoyed the hell out of it.
That’s when I met the monsters.
Not the ones under the bed, but the kind that live in possibility the versions of yourself you’d rather not consider, but that still remain entirely possible. Monsters are just possibilities living on the edge of your perception, waiting for the right moment to slip in.
If you happen to see one really see one, smell its breath, feel its presence it’s probably just lost. That’s why they look so ferocious. They’re scared. More scared of you than you are of them.
It’s the monsters you don’t see that should worry you.
 They’re not afraid at all.
 They know you can’t see them.
And maybe that’s what this is the invisible monster of a life that doesn’t align neatly with the world. The kind that refuses to be easily categorized, easily hired, easily explained.
Maybe that’s the price of choosing to live an interesting experience.

prompt:
It became a running joke,
Thinking I can be a writer who drinks,
Not a drinker who writes.
Could I ever write down what we just said?
The truth flares bright between us,
Then vanishes, baby, vanishes instead.

Rule number one  I scrawl in ink:
Don’t start from what you’re not.
Blueprints for a better me?
Tried it. Failed. Forgot.

If everyone planted a garden here,
Nobody would go hungry, dear.
Some grow weeds, some grow gold,
The rest of us trade what we’ve been told.

This is my evil plan yeah!
Grow tomatoes, then the frying pan,
Be the Lizard King if I damn well can.
Not just normal, baby, I wanna be grand.
Sing poems at the dive bar, write checks I can’t cash,
Do yoga, drink whiskey, make a mad dash.

He said he was the Lizard King…
Well, me too, I swing like a pendulum thing.
He called me Lizard Queen, I laughed 
Then lost myself inside a draft.
(Draft of what? Doesn’t matter, still a writer, still a scatter)

Sudden lurch, a page goes missing
I was profound, now I’m pissin'
In a stranger’s house again
Oh well. Start over, grab a pen

The sublime and the stupid side by side.
A burlesque of truth I no longer hide.
I don’t want safe. I want fun.
I want to strip down in the midday sun.
Wear the crazy thing like it's my skin
Pretend it’s my first time again.

[Chorus 2 – Rising tempo]
This is my evil plan! 
Grow zucchinis in a coffee can,
Channel ghosts from a soda stand,
Be Beer Garden royalty, bare feet in the sand.
Write epiphanies in traffic, burn bridges with flair,
Treat strangers like prophets pretend I care.

What happens?
(What happens?)
What happens when I stop pretending?
(Stop pretending!)
What happens when the beat keeps lending
Me a life I can dance in,
A life I can end in.

This is my evil plan to grow what I can,
In a beer-garden town with a notebook in hand.
Don’t want to be a brand, don’t want to be bland,
Let me be strange this is my evil plan.
Not perfect, not polished, just real as I am,
Let me be messy, let me be grand,
Let me begin this is my evil plan.

Stand up straight.
That’s the start.
That’s the whole damn plan.
(yeah… yeah…)
Stand up straight.
That’s the start.
That’s the whole damn plan.
[fade out on organ swirl and heartbeat drum]

prompt:
I wrote a comment at 3 A.M.,
Sharp as a tack, a digital gem.
Posted it once, refreshed the page…
Zero likes, my tiny stage.

I could write a screen play, a cinematic feat
'Bout the time I dropped gold on the internet street.
A heart felt performance, a tragedy-slash-farce
About shouting my genius at the cold universe.
It's a one-woman show in a theater so grand,
"The Comment No One Saw," coming soon to on-demand!

Buried alive under a thousand takes,

About how I posted brilliance

Below "Like if you're watching in twenty twenty five."

About how my words got swallowed
By the endless tide.

And thank the crowd,

That I typed out loud.

Nobody saw it.
Except me…
Refreshing endlessly.

prompt:
My Evil Plan

It became a running joke, whether I could ever write down what we’d just discussed. Ideas flare up, brilliant and certain in the air between us, then vanish like smoke the moment my pen touches the page.
So, this is the plan: capture the smoke.

The plan has rules.
Rule number one: Don’t start from what you are not.
So many people try to build from the clean, sensible version of themselves they wish existed. I’ve done it too, sketched the blueprints for a better me, then failed spectacularly. This isn’t that. This is an inventory of the glorious, cluttered mess already here.

The foundation of the plan is what I call the Beer Garden Theory.
It’s simple: if everyone in this part of town grew a garden, nobody would starve.
Someone would say, “But some people would grow a bad garden!” and to that, the plan says, “Others would teach them.” For the community benefit. We’d trade tomatoes for technique, zucchini for wisdom. It’s a beautiful thought: a world where everyone helps each other tend their plots. Maybe share a six-pack of something nicely crafted.

But then my own faulty wiring trips the circuit.
I don’t want to be normal.
I want to be exciting.

So, he thought he was the Lizard King, and if he was, then so am I. I feel the psychological pendulum of the soul swing wide. One moment I’m channeling something ancient, sketching the angle of an angel still waiting to land. The next, I’m taking a dump at a stranger’s barbecue, staring into the low flow plumbing and wondering about the fragility of modern design.

That’s the point, isn’t it? The engine of all stories, what happens next?
The plan is to accept that the sublime and the ridiculous always happen simultaneously. You can have a spiritual awakening while being the idiot who doesn’t know what he’s doing.

The performance of self is exhausting.
It’s a burlesque show where every layer you strip off reveals another costume. Could be a different character each time. People see this and say, “multiple personalities,” which sounds marketable, I guess. But it’s simpler, and stranger, than that. It’s just trying to find the right way to be.
Pretend it’s your first time. Wear the crazy thing.

But then the dark moments come, caught by circumstances too easy to deny. You take them. And in taking them, you have to decide who to be loyal to.
Can you really be drunk and focused on the same time, man?
I go to the bar with my notebook, thinking I can be a writer who drinks instead of a drinker who writes. But the calm, the one that rises in my chest and slows my breath, can be found in whiskey or in yoga. Meditation or medication. What’s the difference? One feels like someone else medicating me; the other’s just me, doing it myself.

The worst of it was walking into the university to fill out a job application, completely unmoored after an hour of aimless driving. I didn’t know where I was going or why. Afraid of going home to myself. Not wanting to drink again because I knew where that road leads the ruin of authorship, the bone-cracking anxiety, the fuzz and whir in my body, all in the name of some warped defense of freedom.

And then, a breakthrough.
A posture epiphany.
Shoulders down. Pelvis open. A small, physical shift that changes everything. You wonder why you’re not getting what you want, and maybe the answer is just to treat people like they’re your best friend. Maybe the answer is realizing you are your own mother. Which, honestly, explains a lot.

I’m trying to write down what I said.
If I could just figure out how to write it down, I think I could save myself. But the words are slippery. Still, I recognize her in me the one looking out through my own eyes. I know she will survive.

This plan my evil, beautiful, impossible plan is simply to let her.
To harmonize with the me inside me instead of lamenting her.
To ask what it even means to be an American girl these days remembering that we were told we could be anything, still smelling the faint salt of oceans from the 70s and 80s and to just stand up straight.

That’s the start.
That’s the whole plan.

title: I Took the Bus to a Topless Bar
tags: danceable, infectious, punk cabaret, disco-pop, fluid, melodic hook, infectious rhythm, fuzz guitar, layered texture, harmonized, melodic hook, perfect EQ, fast flow, fast flow, cheeky, playful, funky bass, disco guitars, punchy drums, lounge, Vocals: Female lead, smoky, but charming, mischievous, detached but occasionally soaring, emotive, yet restrained, a female voice, intimate vocal quality, voice is clear and articulate, confident, ironic flair, dirty, sexy female vocals,
prompt:
It felt like the first time doing anything 
First speech, first show, first kiss, ring.
Kinda like the first time public speakin'
Climb up trembling to a mic that's squeakin.
Like school buses, first crushes, lipstick on wrong 
The kind of thing that writes its own song.

I took the bus to a topless bar,
Shopped all morning for heels and charm.
Smoke hit first, then sound, then dark 
A lounge full of perfume and question marks.
Smoke and music swallowed the door,
A soda in hand, nerves on the floor.
Dark lounge, velvet lies,
Watched the girls with cautious eyes.

The bouncer blinked, I filled the form,
Backstage nerves in classic storm.
Said, “I don’t have clothes", which was a lie,
But nerves don’t care. They just deny.
He sold me a bikini for cash I lacked,
Said I could pay it back once I was back in the black.
Bright mango bikini, last in my size!
Didn’t match my skin but it matched my rise.

So I changed into neon, ready or not 
Too tight, too bright, but it’s what I got.

Back in the dark, mirror-lit room,
Fidgeted hard like I’d burst too soon.
DJ said, “What lights, what tracks?”
I said “No country” and watched him laugh.
A man leaned in smooth like he knew the script 
Said I looked lovely, voice sugar-dipped.

I told him, “Yeah, I’m new today.”
Never even been in a topless place.
He said “You’ll do fine,” and gave a grin,
Then left me alone with the lights and sin.

They called my name - I rose like breath,
Like I could dodge regret and death.

Didn’t know the floor was slick as oil,
Moved too fast in a nervous coil.
Boots hit floor, heart hit spine,
I launched too fast, missed the line.
Didn’t fall cute, didn’t land slick.
Veered too wide, did a slapstick trick.
Even in that flailing pose, 
I moved with gusto heaven knows
Spun round the pole, slipped like sin,
Gravity flirted - I let it win.

A girl in rhinestones pulled me near,
Whispered close in my ear:
“You don’t gotta dance - just tease.
Look at ‘em like you wanna buckle their knees.
That’s all it takes. Not grace, not form.
Just a bit of nerve and a ‘come-hither’ storm."

With gusto, I hit that floor,
Slid like hell and came back for more.
I didn’t crush - I didn’t quit,
And damn, I gotta say: I liked that shit.

I had never been in a place like that.
Never stood on a stage with just nerve and a rented thong.
But I didn’t run.
I slipped.
I spun.

[Reprise]
With gusto, I lost control,
Laughed mid-fall and owned the role.
Boots hit floor, heart hit spine,
I launched too fast, missed the line.
Didn’t fall cute, didn’t land slick.
Veered too wide, did a slapstick trick.
But honey, even on my knees,
I milked applause like striptease cheese.

[Chorus – Punk Cabaret Style]
With gusto, I hit that floor,
Slid like hell and came back for more.
I was green, I was loud,
With one tit out, still damn proud
Didn’t win, but I owned that stage 
Like a saint in fishnets, center cage.
No grace, no fame, no starry name,
Just glitter, guts, and a holy flame.
Didn’t nail it, didn’t care 
I made that stage my own affair.
I didn’t crush, I didn’t quit,
And damn, I gotta say: I liked that shit.

I wished I knew you better, you wished the same of me,
so, I wrote this broken letter, and I left it in the sea.

I name them when I’m lonely, and I answer when I hear.

like a psalm with a knife in the rhyme.
I carry it carefully, carry
and it carries me most of the time.

the easy road kept calling, but I stepped across the sign.

a silence long as winter that still warms the face.

like a vow that won’t quite align.

and it carries me most of the time.

the jukebox hums a witness, the night counts on its thumbs.

small fire in a dark room shows you where you are.

like a lantern that won’t fully shine.
I carry it carefully, carry
and it carries me most of the time.

when the border becomes the design.
I carry it carefully, carry
and it carries me most of the time.

my fear with a covenant shine.
I carry it carefully, carry
and it carries me, most of the time.

prompt:
[Verse 1]
How do I quote myself, thinking I got something real?
Thinking I got something good to offer,
To the ones I’m trying to heal.

Variety is still the spice of life.

My head is swimming, haven’t touched the snow in two days.

Six times a day for months, maybe more.
Time gets lost, like loose change on the barroom floor.

[Chorus]
The entertainment for everyone, cracked open on the shelf.
Trying to quiet the storm inside, just trying to quell myself.

You really wanna know someone? Watch ‘em unpack their shit.
The purse, the pain, the cigarettes, what they choose to admit.
It ain’t the one who helps you move,
It’s the one who sees your mess and still makes room.

Beer and smoke help, sure.
But have you ever questioned your motivation?
Fell headlong into your expectations,
And had to admit
You might just be a twisted individual.

[Bridge 1 – Creeping bassline under this]
Maybe alcoholics and drug addicts became cynical, angry individuals not because they were doomed, but because their environment never allowed them to see the sick, mean, self-serving, power-hungry, manipulative person they already were.

[Verse 4]
Valentine’s came, bouquet showed up at the bar.
I wasn’t even there - imagine that, how bizarre.
Some guy showed me his love archive,
Photos on a bed where heartbreak thrives.
Every caption another cracked-open vein,
And I felt pure joy - him sharing his pain.

[Chorus]
Yeah, I’m interrupted by life, by strangers, by tears,
By stories that mirror my own across years.
Even the tale I was trying to write got paused,
By someone else’s need - and honestly, I applaud.

[Verse 5]
I used to never drink, never touch a thing.
Now I’m ticking off vices like a goddamn king.
Marijuana, vodka, cocaine, wooden spoon,
All that just to be myself by afternoon.

[Refrain – like a punchline]
I’m so horny it’s biblical.

P H D in philosophy and nothing left to lose.

[Bridge 2]
“Well shit man, you’re a regular fixture.

Every drunk in here asks for meaning
Between shots and self-defeating.

I’m the regular fixture now, neon-lit and worn,
A prophet in a dive bar, equal parts loved and torn.
I don’t run, I don’t confess - I just keep playing through,
A mirror held up to the mess. And baby, right now that mess is you.

Pour one more for the holy wrecks,
The half-healed hearts and broken necks.
I’ll raise my glass to the jukebox choir
Saints of smoke and stolen fire.

Tip your bar tender.

prompt:
How do I quote myself? thinking I have something positive to offer the ones I’m thinking of? I find different ways to do it. Variety is still the spice of life.

My head is swimming. I’ve been sober more often in the past three days than I have in a few months. Haven’t indulged in the nose candy for a whole two days. 

Waste feels a lot better. 

I’ve been doing it at least six times a day for the past couple months. Maybe longer. The concept of time gets lost.

The counselor for everyone. And yet, I get cracked with guilt and spin over my own chaos. The process to quell myself.

I could easily escape. I could take my chances with an unthinkable cave of rave. Or keep to myself.  And make it on my own. I think I’ll be making it on my own either case.

The easiest way to get to know someone is to watch them unpack their shit. You’ll find out a lot. 

It’s not that your best friends are the only ones who help you move. It’s the ones who help you unpack your purse that become your best friends.

Beer and smoke help too, of course. So yeah, that’s who I’m cutting this on. Have you ever questioned your motivation? Have you ever failed headlong at your expectations and hid away the fact that you're a twisted individual?

Maybe alcoholics and drug addicts became cynical, angry individuals not because they were doomed, but because their environment never allowed them to see the sick, mean, self-serving, power-hungry, manipulative person that they already were.

So, Valentine’s Day came and went. My boyfriend or whatever sent this enormous bouquet of roses and lilies for me. He sent it to the bar, of course. 

Hey, I’m not there right now. Imagine that. 

Constant interruptions. But worthwhile interruptions, at least.

Wow. Almost moved to tears as this dude shows me his collection. Each one, a photo that he had on the bed since Valentine’s, immersed in the red and open compilation. Each sentiment attached has been shared with me. I feel a moment of pressure and abstraction at the beauty of learning about other people. The value of letting myself be interrupted.

Even the story I was trying to tell. A worthwhile interruption. Writing this makes me feel the same way. Pure joy in sharing.

He was impressed with my answer and even though he was sort of a loser, I was happy. I was impressed with myself. Ha ha. Honestly.

I had to laugh a couple weeks ago. I was here at the bar, thinking about how I used to never use any drugs, never drink. And through my mind I went through the list of things I had done just that very day. 

So many things I said I’d never do, all of them.

The dude wants something illicit: 

Marijuana. Vodka. Cocaine. Wooden spoon. Isn’t that crazy? 
Took all that just to make me myself again.

I’m so horny. It’s all I can think about. Just fucking. Fucking. Fucking. I just want to fuck and I don’t even want this guy to have my number. 

If I can’t have sex, I might as well have grease. I’m gonna go get a cheeseburger.

So, all I’m doing is telling you all the shit that I already know, and if not makes me sad that you don’t, plus my hands are sick of hearing it, so let’s tell you.

I decided to talk to Dirk one day or rather let him talk since he wasn’t nodding off at the bar.

Fucking Darlene. She always misses her pool game ‘cause she spends so much time in the bathroom. Then she gets all pissed off. What a waste of energy.

And oh— “Did I ever beat that guy at pool?” he asked me. “Yeah, once,” I said. “Did he squeeze your hand really hard after?”

I shrugged.

“I dunno. If you squeeze hard first they can’t get you like that.”

He’s always talking about blood coming out of his eyes. He couldn’t write either unless he was drinking.

I got shot a game. The guy I was playing had a terribly obnoxious lack of personality. He’s wandering around the bar now wondering why I blew him off when I’m so nice to everyone else.

He has a PhD in philosophy. No wonder he’s developed a heroin habit. And pills. He gets them from the VA. 

How else could he afford to sit at this bar day in, day out? He was pissed at me a few months back because I never acknowledged him. Finally he confronts me on it and I retort:

“Well shit man, you’re a regular fixture here. Do I greet the jukebox too?”

title: Oh, The Things You'll Delay (An Edgy, Midlife-Realist Parody)
tags: deep sexy female vocal, cutecore,  punchy bass, dynamic flow, dynamic drops, fast flow,, bright synths, smooth flow, bedroom pop, miami bass, idol, complex, trip, drop, punchy bass, catchy guitar riffs, harmonized, melodic hook, funky slap bass, crisp snares, noir, captivating, trip, vibrant synths, innovative, impact, smooth flow, future rave, punchy drums
prompt:
Congratulations!
Today is… a lot.
You’re off to do something!
(Or maybe you’re not.)

You have brains in your head.
You have shoes by the door.
You have fourteen unread texts
you continue to ignore.

You can steer yourself
any direction you please
as long as it’s one
that doesn’t need a pass, please.

You’re on your own!
And you know what you know!
Which is mostly your passwords
and three kinds of woe.

You’ll look up from your phone.
You’ll think, “Today’s the day!”
Then remember you scheduled
a full-blown delay.

Some paths you won’t choose.
They involve outdoors.
Other roads lead to people
hard no, closed doors.

With your head full of thoughts
and your gut full of toast,
you’ll draft a bold plan
then immediately ghost.

And when all the streets
seem suspect or weird,
you’ll take the one marked:
“NOPE. Too many ring lights.”

“It’s open over there!”
some influencer yells.
But you’re still on the couch
reading Yelp reviews of hell.

Out there, things can happen!
And they might happen to you!
But only if you close Slack
and exit that queue.

When things start to happen,
don’t stew. Don’t fret.
Just panic on mute
and pretend you can hear it.

Oh, the things you’ll delay!
The naps you’ll defend!
The voice memos labeled:
“Someday. Maybe. Send?”

You’ll be up on your way!
You’ll be riding the wave!
Then immediately crash
because you forgot to save.

You won’t lag behind
you’ll just “strategically pause.”
You’ll say “I’m in process,”
which is burnout with cause.

Wherever you go,
you’ll be medium great!
And that’s honestly fine
greatness can wait.

Except when it wont
Because sometimes it won’t.
Sometimes your ambition
gets stuck in your throat.

Bang-ups and hang-ups?
Oh, yes, they will greet you.
You’ll RSVP “Maybe,”
then delete who tried to meet you.

You’ll land in a Slump
where your blanket’s a cloak
and your last accomplishment
was one decent joke.

Un-slumping yourself
takes two feral screams
and three half-finished hobbies
you disguised as “dreams.”

You’ll stumble through crossroads
with unclear signs.
One says “Legacy,”
the other: “More Vines?”

Do you stay on the path
or rebrand your name?
Do you keep saying “yes”
or finally draw lines?

You’ll run through the fog
on fumes and dread,
chasing a vision
you almost made clear.

And then you will reach…
The Waiting Place.
Where hope and panic
sit face to face.

Waiting for clarity.
Waiting for chill.
Waiting for someone
to Venmo the bill.

Waiting for seasons.
Waiting for hair.
Waiting to care
if you even still care.

Waiting for answers
to write themselves clean.
Waiting for Plot
like you’re seventeen.

Everyone is just waiting.

But you?
Nah. You’ll snap.
You’ll order a mic
and drop a sad rap.

You’ll throw out your planner
and write on your walls.
You’ll ignore group texts
and return five missed calls.

You’ll flinch and proceed.
You’ll pitch weird ideas.
You’ll say “I’m not okay”
then sell merch with that shtick.

Oh, the jokes you’ll make up!
There’s healing in pun!
There’s power in saying,
“FINE. I’m not done.”

You’ll build something scrappy.
You’ll stand there, off-script.
You’ll get one weird message:
“Hey, that actually hit.”

You’ll cringe at old posts
but keep making them still.
You’ll start finding joy
right next to “free will.”
 Statistically speaking? Sure
 Possibly
 Kid, you’ll move something, even if it’s just chairs
 Or your own damn expectations down a few stairs

So be your name Burnout,
or Bixby, or Rae,
your inbox is waiting
just… hand it in today.

prompt:
Congratulations!
Today is your day.
You’re off to Great Places!
You’re off and away!

You have brains in your head.
You have feet in your shoes.
You can steer yourself any direction you choose.
You’re on your own. And you know what you know. And YOU are the guy who’ll decide where to go.

You’ll look up and down streets. Look’em over with care. About some you will say, “I don’t choose to go there.” With your head full of brains and your shoes full of feet, you’re too smart to go down a not-so-good street.

And you may not find any you’ll want to go down. In that case, of course, you’ll head straight out of town. It’s opener there in the wide open air.

Out there things can happen and frequently do to people as brainy and footsy as you.

And when things start to happen, don’t worry. Don’t stew. Just go right along. You’ll start happening too.

Oh! The Places You’ll Go!

You’ll be on your way up!
You’ll be seeing great sights!
You’ll join the high fliers who soar to high heights.

You won’t lag behind, because you’ll have the speed. You’ll pass the whole gang and you’ll soon take the lead. Wherever you fly, you’ll be best of the best. Wherever you go, you will top all the rest.

Except when you don’t.
Because, sometimes, you won’t.


I’m sorry to say so but, sadly, it’s true that Bang-ups and Hang-ups can happen to you.

You can get all hung up in a prickle-ly perch. And your gang will fly on. You’ll be left in a Lurch.

You’ll come down from the Lurch with an unpleasant bump. And the chances are, then, that you’ll be in a Slump.

And when you’re in a Slump, you’re not in for much fun. Un-slumping yourself is not easily done.

You will come to a place where the streets are not marked. Some windows are lighted. But mostly they’re darked. A place you could sprain both your elbow and chin! Do you dare to stay out? Do you dare to go in? How much can you lose? How much can you win?

And if you go in, should you turn left or right…or right-and-three-quarters? Or, maybe, not quite? Or go around back and sneak in from behind? Simple it’s not, I’m afraid you will find, for a mind-maker-upper to make up his mind.
You can get so confused that you’ll start in to race down long wiggled roads at a break-necking pace and grind on for miles across weirdish wild space, headed, I fear, toward a most useless place.

The Waiting Place…for people just waiting.

Waiting for a train to go or a bus to come, or a plane to go or the mail to come, or the rain to go or the phone to ring, or the snow to snow or waiting around for a Yes or No or waiting for their hair to grow. Everyone is just waiting.

Waiting for the fish to bite or waiting for wind to fly a kite or waiting around for Friday night or waiting, perhaps, for their Uncle Jake or a pot to boil, or a Better Break or a string of pearls, or a pair of pants or a wig with curls, or Another Chance. Everyone is just waiting.

No! That’s not for you!
Somehow you’ll escape all that waiting and staying. You’ll find the bright places where Boom Bands are playing. With banner flip-flapping, once more you’ll ride high! Ready for anything under the sky. Ready because you’re that kind of a guy!


 Oh, the places you’ll go! There is fun to be done! There are points to be scored. There are games to be won. And the magical things you can do with that ball will make you the winning-est winner of all. Fame! You’ll be famous as famous can be, with the whole wide world watching you win on TV.

Except when they don’t. Because, sometimes, they won’t.

I’m afraid that some times you’ll play lonely games too. Games you can’t win ‘cause you’ll play against you.

All Alone!
Whether you like it or not, Alone will be something you’ll be quite a lot.

And when you’re alone, there’s a very good chance you’ll meet things that scare you right out of your pants. There are some, down the road between hither and yon, that can scare you so much you won’t want to go on.

But on you will go though the weather be foul. On you will go though your enemies prowl. On you will go though the Hakken-Kraks howl. Onward up many a frightening creek, though your arms may get sore and your sneakers may leak. On and on you will hike. And I know you’ll hike far and face up to your problems whatever they are.

You’ll get mixed up, of course, as you already know. You’ll get mixed up with many strange birds as you go. So be sure when you step. Step with care and great tact and remember that Life’s a Great Balancing Act. Just never forget to be dexterous and deft. And never mix up your right foot with your left.

And will you succeed?
Yes! You will, indeed!
(98 and ¾ percent guaranteed.)

Kid, you’ll move mountains!
So…be your name Buxbaum or Bixby or Bray or Mordecai Ale Van Allen O’Shea, you’re off to Great Places!
Today is your day!
Your mountain is waiting.
So…get on your way!

Thirteen came with shackles, not a cake

Boot camp, group home, JDC

Each night a script I’d memorize
Don’t speak too loud, don’t break your role
Survival's quiet, numb, and cold

prompt:
[driving industrial-rock groove, glitchy synth undercurrent, guitars snarling like data packets on fire]

[Verse 1]
Neon halo in a midnight inbox,
Wish-bone trigger pulled by phantom bots.
Thought the cosmos cracked a grin my way
Turns out it’s just the backend of a payday.
Love-letter pop-ups dressed as destiny,
I clicked yes and signed away the best of me.

[Pre-Chorus]
Silicon saints whisper “Amen, engage.”
Miracles merchandised page by page.

[Chorus]
This ain’t divine intervention
It’s a funnel with a holy disguise.
Got my faith in suspension,
Scrolling through manufactured highs.
If the universe talks in a banner ad’s roar,
Then my prayers hit the spam box floor.
Yeah, the algorithm of awe
Keeps selling me back my soul.

[Verse 2]
Street-corner prophet with a QR code,
Preaching cashback karma on a social scroll.
Serendipity’s been siphoned, sold,
Wrapped in velvet rhetoric, two for gold.
Every “meant-to-be” now a metrics scheme,
Pixel-perfect predators haunting every dream.

[Pre-Chorus 2]
Gut feeling glitching, buffer, delay
Heaven’s paywall says, “Upgrade to pray.”

[Chorus 2]
This ain’t divine intervention
It’s a funnel with a holy disguise.
Got my faith in suspension,
Scrolling through manufactured highs.
When coincidence breaks like a sponsored wave,
Even angels feel click-through depraved.
Yeah, the algorithm of awe
Keeps renting me back my hope.

[Bridge – Spoken Word / Half-rap]
Cut the cord, pull the plug
Hear the silence beyond the buzz.
Give me one raw thunderclap
Not translated into purchase paths.
Let the cosmos crash my feed
No referral links, no greed
Just a pulse that isn’t priced,
A wonder no wallet can slice.

[Breakdown – whisper-to-scream]
Is there any magic left
That can’t be monetized.
Any inner voice
Not yet digitized.

[Final Chorus – double-time]
‘Cause I’m done with counterfeit ecstasies,
With miracles in monthly fees.
Gonna firewall my heartache,
Pirate back my prophecy.
When the algorithm of awe
Stops charging me to believe,
I’ll meet the universe offline
Raw, untagged, and free.

[Outro – fading chant]
No more ads on my divinity,
No more tags on infinity.
Unplugged, I’ll find what’s real
A miracle they can’t steal.

prompt:
[Verse 1]
I’ve been making art outta fractured stars,
Digging up pieces of me from Saturn's back yard.
Found a box labeled “Do Not Open Emotional Risk,”
Guess what? I did.
Been schooling myself in the mirror’s glow,
Setting boundaries like stop signs in fresh-fallen snow.
I’m healing old wounds like a time-traveling nurse,
Learning to love the mess, not just rehearse.

Curiosity’s got me clicking every tab,
PowerPoint buttons I never knew I had.

I’m the factotum dream, a side hustle queen,

Wrangled wild futures with Powerpoint toys.
Learned how to market, how to animate hope,
And how to submit job app number 403 without losing scope.
I serve dreamers with plans that shine
Just give me a whiteboard and a deadline.
I’ll organize your closet or your consciousness
Behind-the-scenes goddess, chaos-blessed.

[Bridge]
You want grit? I’ve got glitter in mine.
I’m the action behind every half-baked sign.
Not risk-averse, just plot-prepared,
And if no one hires me-I’m still out there.
Doing it. Building it. Belting it out.
Wearing my résumé like a thrifted shout.

So if you’re the one with the plan I crave,
I'll lift the load, make bold look brave.

With my scarves, my skills, and every damn thought.
Call it madness or divine recursion
I'm the comeback queen in perpetual version.

Found myself on the edge of the galaxy,
Now I’m just trying to make that version of me pay rent.

tags: female husky voice, melodic punk, memorable, grindcore, funky basslines, driving basslines, smooth flow, footwork, pulsing bass, psychedelic rap, deep female vocals, relentless, metal rap, slam, swagger, big band jazz, skate punk, distorted guitar, washboard, guitar virtuoso, footwork, brutal deathcore, post-apocalyptic, dangerous
prompt:
Because pretty doesn’t mean soft, and grit doesn’t mean silent.

[Verse 1]
Woke up with a plan and a glitch in my brain,
Caffeine for blood, ambition untamed.
They call it chaos
I call it a moodboard.
I patch up my past with a staple gun,
Make my peace, then make it run.
I’ve been broke, but never boring
Always two clicks from soaring.

[Pre-Chorus]
I don’t do tidy, I do true,
Got gold leaf in my residue.
Scarred hands, sharp wit
You best believe there’s glitter in my grit.

[Chorus]
I shine on the edges, cut from the core,
Blaze like a busted-open metaphor.
Wreckage chic and duct-taped divine,
Dust on my boots but the sparkle’s mine.
You want polished? You’ll get raw.
Pretty tough with a rebel claw.
I fall, I spit, I reinvent
Glitter in my grit, every damn percent.

[Verse 2]
I’ve worked ten gigs and wore ten hats,
Made magic out of “can’t” and “that’s just facts.”
I’m not your muse, I’m your exit plan,
When it’s all on fire, I still stand.
Learned the software, fixed the leak,
Fought imposter thoughts every week.
Turned a breakdown into branding,
Now I’m glitter-bomb commanding.

[Bridge – half spoken, half snarled]
This isn’t lipstick on a crisis.
This is warpaint with vices.
My hustle’s not cute, it’s calibrated.
Every cracked mirror’s celebrated.

[Final Chorus]
I shine on the edges, cut from the core,
Too bold for cubicles, too loud to ignore.
Rough draft heart in a sequin vest,
Bet against me; you’ll regret that guess.
I climb, I bleed, I rewrite the script
There’s always glitter in my grit.

[Outro – soft and slow like a warning]
So don’t confuse the shimmer for ease
Every sparkle’s earned.
Every scar has teeth.

prompt:
[Verse 1]
A message lands in crack-of-dawn italics:
“Old friend showed up again, my weekend’s gone metallic.
A couple puffs make the walls turn velvet,
but once it fades, the silence howls, can’t shelve it.
Boredom’s a muscle I forgot how to flex;
now it twitches like a lie-detector wrapped around my neck.”

[Pre-Chorus A]
Empty slots on the online wheel,
no dopamine deal, just the flat click, *feel.*
She’s asking, *“Can I make it without the glass?*
*Or will the mirror cut me back?”*

[Chorus]
Focus on someone else for a minute
see the puppet strings and the fingerprints in it.
He cooks his own clientele, sells the key to the cell;
calls it love, marks it up, keeps the ledger to himself.
He should be chained behind bars of his own design,
but the city lights blur and the sirens stay blind.

[Verse 2]
Seven long winters locked in his smoke;
she found the love-letter crime scene he wrote and never spoke.
Breath stolen, story sealed inside a bag,
evidence too damning for the courthouse flag.
There’s a daughter in a world all her own,
extreme-spectrum galaxy, a mother’s monotone.
Now unemployment gnaws at the rent-thin door,
while he sells escape at triple cost; same store.

[Pre-Chorus B]
She went no-contact, ghost in revolt,
but ghosts need a map when the night patrols.
If she slips, who will bring her the fix-free dawn?
A friend’s hands shake with the question drawn.

[Chorus (repeat)]
Focus on someone else for a minute
see the puppet strings and the fingerprints in it.
He cooks his own clientele, sells the key to the cell;
calls it love, marks it up, keeps the ledger to himself.
He should be chained behind bars of his own design,
but the city lights blur and the sirens stay blind.

[Bridge (spoken-word over low bass & heartbeat drum)
“Brother by choice, or is that glue?
Dealer plants addictions like landmines
waits for the click under your shoe.
Boredom is the crater after the blast,
quiet enough to hear the future ask:
*Will you crawl or will you rise?*
*Will you swap the smoke for sky?*”

[Final Chorus (add gospel-harmony lift)]
Focus on someone else for a minute
yeah, lift their name like a flare that’s lit.
Cut the strings, smash the scales, break the corporate grail;
no more queens for that powder monarchy sale.
Lock the dealer, free the dreamers, let the justice bell chime
’cause survival’s not a crime, and healing’s right on time.

[Outro (whispered)
Boredom’s just space where the soul can breathe;
hold that Breath, I let the ghosts leave.

Twenty-thousand jackets dropped at midnight
“Happy birthday, kid, you’re free.”
Paper clips for safety nets,
dorm-room dreams on EBT.

They snap the file shut-case closed, clean slate.
But trauma doesn’t graduate.

What happens after eighteen?
No banners, no band, just a street full of screens.
Locked doors, loan sharks, hospital bills
Welcome to adulting without a drill.
Age-out, fade-out, nobody’s scene,
But I’m still here, still loud
That’s what happens after eighteen.

[VERSE 2]
Guidance counselor said, “Business math
college isn’t in your fate.”
So I courted every hour
till the clock hands cracked beneath the weight.
Judge said, “Cage is where you fit.”
I mailed him clippings of the Dean’s List,
Watched my rage ignite the pages
Call it pyrotechnic bliss.

[PRE-CHORUS 2]
Anger can be gasoline,
Burn or drive-pick your machine.

[CHORUS (repeat)]
What happens after eighteen?
No banners, no band, just a street full of screens.
Locked doors, loan sharks, hospital bills
Welcome to adulting without a drill.
Age-out, fade-out, nobody’s scene,
But I’m still here, still loud
That’s what happens after eighteen.

55 percent graduate high school-coin flip.
Three percent finish college, paper-thin script.
One in five find a bed on concrete,
One in four taste the justice machine.
But stats don’t measure long-term scars
Attachment issues in empty bars,
PTSD that waits till you name your kid,
Identity crises the census never did.
So knock, knock, knock till the door hinge bends,
Curiosity’s a crowbar, pry till it ends.
You are not broken; you’re under-explained.
Rewrite the data, engrave your name.

What happens after eighteen?

Cold wind, blank map, but an iron spleen.
Turn rage into rocket fuel, scars into steel

Age-out, fade-out? Not my scene.

Yeah, I’m still here, still proud
That’s what happens
That’s what can happen
after eighteen.

Age-out…
Fade-out?
Only if you let them write the refrain

title: AGAINST RECOMMENDATION (Story Time!)
tags: sexy female, sweet female vocals, fast flow, nuanced, unique, sophisticated, complex, honest, masterpiece, textured, sharp, rebellion, unsettling, urgent, overdrive, dynamic vocals, wall of sound, pulsing, poignant, upbeat rhythm, :(adhd):, memorable, neon, iconic
prompt:
[Spoken]
[Solo performance piece, Slam-monologue style.]

I was state property by thirteen.
Stamped, filed, delivered
to foster home one, then two,
boot camp three, juvie four,
group homes five and six
each a new name on the door,
none of them mine.

By eighteen, I had become
a portfolio of case notes,
seven, maybe eight placements deep,
depending on who was counting.
But me?
I was counting days.
To freedom.

The summer before senior year,
my grandmother raised her hand.
"I’ll take her in," she said.
Blood offered blood.
I begged the caseworker
Let me go. Let me live. Let me be.

She said no.

But stay,
she promised me benefits:
Financial aid at 18.
Scholarships. Subsidies.
Just. One. More. Year.

So I stayed.
Set my jaw like concrete
and played the game.

Junior and senior year
I showed potential.
First time anyone said that about me
without a clipboard in their hand.
I signed up for the SAT,
even though my foster home
offered no rides, no prep, no encouragement
just silence and suspicion.

But I did it anyway.

Then came November.
I walked in from school,
found my foster mother’s sister
in my room
the cheer coach
screaming at me about rumors
I never spread.

Newsflash: I was too self-absorbed
to care about your petty soap opera.
But here we were,
her finger in my face,
her sister backing her up,
tag-teaming my dignity.

I tried to leave.
They blocked the door.
So I climbed out the window.

That was foster home #8.
Didn’t matter.
Only a few months left,
then freedom, right?

Wrong.

February 1995.
Called out of chemistry class.
Principal’s office.
Caseworker and guidance counselor
waiting like a firing squad of policy.

"We’re recommending you move in with your grandmother."
Now.
Three months before graduation.
Three months before turning 18.

New town.
New school.
New chaos.

I sat there, mouth open,
watching my future get redacted in real time.
After everything
after I stabilized, succeeded, stayed clean
you want to shake the snow globe now?

I walked back into chemistry,
face wrecked with tears.
My teacher pulled me aside.
I told him everything.
He showed up at my hearing.
Stood up for me.
The judge ignored him.

But he tried.
God, he tried.
And in a world of case numbers,
his voice felt like a lighthouse.

There was a foster family nearby
they’d never housed me,
but they knew the system stank.
They introduced me to strangers,
good strangers.
I arranged my own final placement.
My grandmother signed custody to them.
They rented me their basement.
Fifty bucks a month.

I got my first job.
My first car.
A Pontiac T1000,
held together by prayers and rust,
but it moved.

They taught me to drive.
They took me to the DMV.
They showed up.

I graduated.

Got my own place.
Community college.
Then university.
Graduated with honors in ‘99.
Not bad for a system statistic.

Out of all my foster parents,
only one called me again
to ask me to borrow money from her husband
under false pretenses
so she could give it to her parents.

I played along.
Learned my lesson.

Never again.

So I became a data point of defiance.

50% of foster kids never graduate.
So I graduated early.
High honors.
Gold cords.
Kicked the stat in the teeth.

75% end up with legal trouble.
So I went straight edge.
Walked tight lines like I was born for it.

80% can’t stay self-sufficient.
So I built a fortress out of independence.
Needed no one.
Asked for nothing.

I won.

But no one told me
that independence, when overfed,
mutates into loneliness.
That high achievement
doesn’t come with emotional immunity.
That success is not a solvent
for the grief inside.

I took personal responsibility
so seriously
it hurt me.
Quietly.
Professionally.

I survived the system,
but no one warned me
how long I’d keep living
like I was still trying to survive it.

tags: sexy female, sweet female vocals, fast flow, nuanced, unique, sophisticated, complex, honest, masterpiece, textured, sharp, rebellion, unsettling, urgent, overdrive, dynamic vocals, wall of sound, pulsing, poignant, upbeat rhythm, :(adhd):, memorable, neon, iconic
prompt:
[Spoken]
[Solo performance piece, Slam-monologue style.]

Thirteen.
Eighteen.
Seven homes, two group pads, one juvie hold, one wilderness “boot camp.”
Roll call of custody like a rap sheet I never earned.

I didn’t run; the State did.
Picked me up at thirteen, filed me under Temporary Ward-Indefinite.
Said I’d get “services.”
Translation: I became a spreadsheet cell in someone else’s budget.

Caseworker: “Staying in care means college aid, housing vouchers, medical, cha-cha-cha”
Me: Fine. One more year.
I can eat statistics for breakfast if it keeps me alive till eighteen.

But watch this:
Junior year, SAT, no prep books, no quiet corner, foster mom calling me “uppity.”
Still scored.
Potential sighted-first time on record.

November. After school.
Cheer-coach sister barrels into my room
Screaming. Accusing me of rumors I was too self-absorbed to invent.
Foster mom joins; chorus of rage.
Door barricaded.
So I took the window exit.
Glass is honest; drywall lies.

February ’95.
Principal’s office, caseworker, guidance counselor, fluorescent mercy.
Judge will “recommend” I leave current placement three months before graduation,
ship me to Grandma in another town, another school.
Sudden disruption sold as “family reunification.”

Reunification at T-minus 90 days? That’s not care; that’s sabotage.

Chem teacher pulls me aside
Shows up at court, says: “Your Honor, she’ll lose her diploma.”
Judge clocks the compassion, bangs the gavel anyway.

Neighborhood foster family; never my placement; outraged.
They link me to total strangers with a basement.
Grandma signs temporary custody so I stay in-district.
Fifty bucks a month.
First job, first driver’s license, Pontiac T-1000 (burnt-orange rust, $250, miracle on bald tires).
Strangers did the heavy lifting love was supposed to do.

50% of foster youth skip the diploma.
So I graduated with honors.
75% butt heads with the law.
So I stayed stone-cold straight edge and learned statutes by heart.
80 % can’t sustain themselves.
So I became an army of one.
Ask me how self-reliance morphs into self-harm when applause stops.


No foster parent ever checked on me
except one who wanted me to con her husband for cash.
I was her payday; she was my last lesson.
Trust is expensive; hindsight is discounted.

I beat the numbers, walked the stage, framed the degree.
But survival skills don’t retire when danger does.
Peace feels like a setup; calm triggers fight-or-flight.
I know how to win.
Still learning how to exhale.

Thirteen.
Eighteen.
A lifetime crammed between those digits.

Judge said “Against recommendation, release to grandmother.”
I say “Against odds, release to myself.”

Thirteenth floor
children’s psych ward, Mercy Hospital,

accuracy matters when you’re cataloguing trauma.
Steel-framed windows, wire mesh, institutional dusk.
Thirty-day observation, no pills, no voltage.

Reentry with an anger hotter than the river below.

A war over yogurt.
Expired dairy, fresh fury

because that’s what happens when childhood and early motherhood overlap:
the calendar folds and nobody knows who’s the adult.

No mall. No mission.

Freedom: an empty Chevy, a mutable horizon,

Laughter detonates; ego soot clings to family portraits.

prompt:
One thing I can say is that I have provided a measure of stability for my child. But what I didn’t even think about was the fact that OTHER people move away. When I was a kid, it was just me moving so I never realized that other people are me. Nathan has seen a lot of people move away, os see.. Remember me saying thaty I divorced because I was afraid to become a raging drunk? Well, I didn’t want Nathan exposed to that. title: Reading this probably won’t change your
tags: sexy female, quirky, mischievous, syncopated drums, bouncy bass,  playful, Vintage synths, quirky hooks, witty, teasing, cheeky harmonies, twisted, lighthearted, danceable groove
prompt:
Reading this probably won’t change your life. I have no advice to offer, and even if I do, the world today is actually quite different than it was 20 years ago when these were my circumstances. If I were forced, right now, to claim that this story contains a message of hope, that message would reed:

"If I can become part of the status quo, so can you!"

I'm afraid that is the best I can offer at the moment. I currently have $85,000 in student loan debt. I have problems with motivation, impulse control and…

Ask for guidance on how to proceed. Ask for guidance in formulating your intention in the first place. There may be nothing magical to the result. I ask spirit for guidance, I receive information that informs my decisions, I make a decision and I attribute part of the result to spirit’s guidance (which is really just me asking)…so maybe Spirit is a question; her symbol a giant question mark.

...staying focused. Growing up, I never knew if I was going to be staying where I was or…actually...I mostly knew I would be going, and so, I learned early on to never get comfortable. I have a hard time forming healthy attachments with people. I WANT to. NOW I want to, but up until very recently, it truly never occurred to me to even consider anyone else, largely because I was very pre-occupied with my own survival. As a result, I am not as practiced at forming and developing healthy relationships as I would like to be.

Through recent hard times and probably too much introspection, I have discovered that no matter how much I think I want to maintain an intimate/romantic relationship, I will eventually begin doing things to make my partner question the security of the relationship. To make him feel as uncertain and unstable as I felt during my formative years.

When I say "as I felt during my formative years", I don’t mean to suggest that I was aware of any of my feelings at the time. I don't remember ever paying attention to how I felt about anything, and of course, I never considered any possible future implications of my circumstances. Memories of most of my childhood are fuzzy, but I'm sure I didn't consider myself very different from anyone else, but then, I really never knew anyone well enough to allow for any accurate comparison. Essentially, constant change left me very isolated, and also unaware of my isolation.

My adolescence was tightly tied in with the bureaucratic machinations of local governments. It does mean something when they say you are a “ward of the state”, and it's certainly nothing glamorous. To make things interesting for myself, I began to fantasize that I lived in some sort of "La Femme Nikata" scenario.

I can recall at least two occasions, very early on in my experience as a newly labeled "Ward of the State of Pennsylvania - Delinquent", when I was taken to undergo psychological testing. One time I was taken to a nearby university, and on another occasion we went to the big city of Pittsburg, PA. The university was, of course, full of neatly dressed academic professionals; and in the city, people had a quickness to their step that made them seem somehow more official than any of the local folks who inhabited the surrounding rural areas, where I had spent most of my life up to that point.

The fact that smart, official-looking people seemed interested in my psychological makeup, and were spending several hours with me, testing my skills and aptitudes, made me feel important (maybe for the first time), and added just enough realism to my nascent coping fantasy to give it a good foothold, and legs to run with. "There must be something special about me", I began to think, "and it’s probably that I am a spy".

Once I became special in my own mind, any emotional pain I might have experienced over my inability to truly connect with anyone, disappeared from my day-to-day awareness. The fantasy that I had some very special mission, and had too many important things to do to be bothered with establishing close ties, served me quite well over the next few years, as I travelled through no less than seven foster homes, at least two group living facilities for children, and one very special boot camp designed to set the incorrigible on the right path; or possibly, to train future spies.
