tags: clear female vocal, droning, noir, masterpiece, polyphonic, hip, chamber ensemble
prompt:
Soft Focus, Hard Time
A paranoid pop‑noir for the age of ambient dread

Street cams bloom like steel magnolias,
⁠LED petals drinking every angle of you.
Resting pulse is yesterday’s fiction
⁠now your heartbeat streams in 4K, too.
Thought you were alone with a notebook?
⁠Cloud sync says otherwise, friend.
Even dreams show up with metadata;
⁠REM‑cycles monetize while you pretend.

Here comes the hush inside the skull
⁠that low hum of “don’t get flagged.”
Freedom feels like open water
⁠till the satellites zig‑zag.

We’re doing soft time in a hard lens,
⁠paying interest on each breath we take.
Smile for the algorithm: it forgets nothing,
⁠and forgiveness is a premium upgrade.
Every gaze is mirrored chrome,
⁠every whisper time‑stamped divine.
History’s written in real time now,
⁠soft focus, hard time.

Draft folder full of dangerous brilliance,
⁠never leaves the quarantine zone.
Creativity files for asylum,
⁠denied: “Insufficient compliance shown.”
Irony’s a contraband substance,
⁠humor wears a counterfeit grin.
When language must lawyer itself,
⁠confession turns corporate within.

The watchdog lives inside the eye,
⁠trained to bark at every spark.
A thousand self‑edits later,
⁠the canvas stays politely dark.

We’re doing soft time in a hard lens…

Privacy’s a luxury condo; priced out.
Kids barter secrets like cigarettes in the yard.
Some go feral for an untracked second,
⁠some hug the rules till the bones turn hard.

Analog nights become folklore,
⁠blackouts worshipped like storms.
Paywalls rise around silence,
⁠quiet’s the newest uniform.

Count the years in notification pings;
trace the evolution of the flinch.
We adapted, we complied
⁠now the cage is native speech.

We’re doing soft time in a hard lens,
⁠chasing shadows of a private mind.
Polish your halo for the watchers,
⁠their memory is diamond‑spined.
If tomorrow lives outside the servers,
⁠meet me there; off‑grid, off‑line.
Till then we serve this velvet sentence:
⁠soft focus, hard time.

Lights never dim, they only pivot.
Blink, and the century blinks back

prompt:

for the right to choose,
But choice don’t mean shit
When none of us can use
Our own damn skin
Without signing a waiver,
Without risking a cage
For a mushroom, or a favor.

Pick a shroom, brew a cup,
Meet the cosmic loom
Get nine months for “contraband,”
Rot in county gloom.
They say we’re free
But look around and see:

Watch your liberty flee.

I call it a cage.

As performative rage.

Cage the home,
Till all that’s left
Is a stripped-down drone.
Pick the wrong pill,
Wrong tea, wrong thrill
And they’ll skin you legal.

Don’t talk about justice
While thousands sit in cells
For tea made from a mushroom
Or an erb with too much smell.

[Verse 5 – Faster pace, rhythmic delivery]
Innocent? Sure, until they say you’re not.
Bail if you’re lucky. Rot if you’re not.
Guilt’s irrelevant.
What matters is cost.
And if you can’t pay,
You just get lost.

[Pre-Chorus – Spoken punch]
If liberty can vanish from a victimless crime,
Then liberty was marketing the whole damn time.

[Chorus – Return, stronger delivery]
Call it order, I see chains.
Manufactured crimes,
Commercial pain.
Cage the body,
Cage the home,
Till all that’s left
Is a stripped-down drone.
Pick the wrong pill,
Wrong tea, wrong thrill
And they’ll skin you legal.

[Verse 6 – Rhythmic spoken slam]
Three thousand four hundred eighty-nine ways
To get arrested for choosing wrong.
Two thousand seven hundred eighty-five things
You’re not allowed to feel good on.
But nobody’s stopping them from being
Cruel.
Greedy.
Armed.
And elected.

[Verse 7 – Slow and deliberate]
Tell me who got saved,
Who's supposed to heal,
When choice becomes
A booking slip,
Orange suits, and steel.

[Pre-Chorus – Spoken punch]
If liberty can vanish from a victimless crime,
Then liberty was marketing the whole damn time.

[Final Chorus – Big finish, full voice]
You can call it law
I call it abuse.
Punished for peace.
Condemned for use.
Cage the body,
Cage the home,
Till all that’s left
Is a stripped-down drone.
Pick the wrong pill,
Wrong tea, wrong thrill
And they’ll skin you legal.

[Outro – Spoken fade, steady cadence]
More rules. Less reason.
More jails. Less freedom.
More names in the system.
Less human in the mirror.

jail in the womb, jail in the vein,
Jail in the tea and the labor pain.
Till we own our nerves, our blood, our breath
Resistance is the only liberty left.

title: JAIL. COMES. HOME.
tags: clear female vocals, deep vocals, industrial, punk, impact,
prompt:
I’m not here to downplay the right
To say no thanks to a life you didn’t ask for.
But let’s not lie to ourselves
You don’t own your body either.
None of us do.
Your skin is leased.
Your blood is indexed.
Your choices are pre-approved, or prosecuted.

Pick a mushroom.
Brew a cup.
Nine months in a cell
For what?
For touching the earth and asking to feel
Something other than dread.

She can’t say no to nine months of pregnancy,
But I can’t say yes to one hour of peace
Without risking a cage.
Without risking a name I don’t want.

You say we’re free.
But I’ve read the fine print.
Freedom costs bail.
And I can’t afford rent.
If choice is contraband,
And calm is a crime
Then we’re all just inmates
Doing time.

They call it law
But it doesn’t protect.
Nobody’s life was at risk.
Nobody was harmed.
But the law came anyway.
Uniformed.
Armed.
Sanctioned.

You can get locked away
For a feeling.
For a vibe.
For a naturally occurring organism
You dared to invite inside.

Victimless crime.
Limitless time.
Booked for fun.
Booked for breath.
Booked for sitting in the wrong kind of peace
At the wrong kind of desk.

You might get out in time to keep your job
If you can pay.
If you can prove you’re not a danger
To the people who wrote the danger.

But if you’re poor?
If you’re brown?
If you’re tired, high, or human?
The cell waits.
The charges wait.
The trauma waits.
But no one tells you how long.
Because the calendar isn’t yours anymore.

You say we’re free.
But I’ve seen the ledger.
Innocent until cashless.
Then forgotten forever.
If choice is illegal
And comfort is banned
Then this isn’t freedom.
It’s a brand.

three thousand four hundred eighty nine ways to be punished
For being alive wrong.
two thousand seven hundred thirty two reasons to cage you
For feeling too strong.

Meanwhile:
No penalty for greed.
No sentence for cruelty.
No time served for hate.
Just power
Elected.
Protected.
Reelected.

This is not about safety.
This is about control.
This is not about victims.
It’s about roles.
They write the script.
We act obedient.
They name it order.
But it’s punishment.

You say we’re free.
But I don’t believe you.
They brought the jail
To the body, the breath, the bedroom.
She’s not behind bars
But she’s not alone.
'Cause when you criminalize choice
Jail comes home.

prompt:
There’s a neon proverb flashin’ on a million mirrored screens,
“Trust your gut, listen close” yeah, we all know what it means.
We click, we nod, we quote it, like a fortune-cookie creed,
Then fall off to the daydreams where no muscle follows the lead.

[Refrain]
But your instinct ain’t a bumper sticker, it’s a pistol startin’ gun;
If you don’t lace up and run, that wisdom’s good for none.

[Verse 2]
You polish up excuses like they’re silver souvenir spoons,
File them in the drawer marked “Later” with your half-forgotten tunes.
But the quiet knock inside you isn’t some romantic ghost
It’s the drumroll for a leap you fear to make the most.

[Verse 3]
Some folks treat intuition like a jukebox in their head
Drop a coin of fantasy, hum the anthem, go to bed.
But a compass left unhandled’s just a pretty piece of brass;
You can frame it in the hallway while you still walk ’round in circles,
kissin’ asphalt, chasin’ glass.

We put our guts on trial, call ’em liars on the stand,
Let the lawyer-brain object till the verdict’s second-hand.
We deport the primal whispers to a dusty attic room,
Then wonder why the floorboards creak a prophecy of doom.

See, the stomach ain’t a trickster, kid, it never swears a false decree.
You can drown it out with spreadsheets, but it keeps its guarantee.
Faith without a footstep? That’s belief that never breathes;
A seed that never splits will never see the leaves.

[Verse 4]
So let the drum inside your ribcage set the cadence for your feet,
Turn the pulse into a passport every time it starts to beat.
Respect ain’t in the daydream, no, it’s waiting in the deed;
The map is nice, but brother, only travel plants the seed.

[Final Refrain]
’Cause a truth you only daydream is a truth you still betray;
Let your instincts steer the wheel, hit the road, don’t just pray.

prompt:
Well, the hangers click like castanets in a panic parade,
While the shoes squat high like bankers on a bonus they never made.
I keep folding my sins into cotton, hoping virtue comes free with the tags
But the closet just laughs, says, “Honey, you’re hauling your past in these bags.”

I bought hope on aisle eight, BILLY bookcase in a box,
Promised “simple assembly” but it fights like paradox.
Allen key preaching Swedish, screws rolling under the bed;
Turns out flat-pack salvation needs spare parts and meds.

Closet chaos, closet creed,
A mausoleum of “must-have” turned confession of need.
Bought another identity on a two-for-one deal
Turns out the zipper jams where the truth won’t kneel.

There’s a jacket from a night when I swore I’d change the world,
Still smells like cheap bourbon and that ex with the half-smile curled.
Scarves hang like surrender flags in a nation built on “someday,”
And the jeans on the floor keep begging for wars my waistline can’t replay.

Oh, the tags whisper hymns of carbon footprints and sweatshop songs,
While I keep swipe-buy-repenting, preaching thrift, doing wrong.

Closet chaos, closet cry,
Every hanger’s a timeline I forgot to untie.
Sweaters in summer, boots in July
Proof I’m hoarding futures that already died.

See, you can color-code your crisis, shove it row by row,
But shame still fits on credit, and regret still loves BOGO.
Hangers snap like promises; boxes break like truth
Belts knot up like headlines strangling a wasted youth.
So I draft another system on a crumpled donation sheet,
Then toss it in with last year’s trends, broken record on repeat.

Maybe I’ll drive it all to Goodwill, trade my chaos in for calm,
But I know I’ll just refill the void, fast fashion’s Trojan bomb.
So I slam the door like Congress does on bills they’ll never read,
Out of sight, out of mind, til tomorrow’s Amazon feed.

Closet chaos, preacher’s note:
You can’t Marie-Kondo the ache in your throat.
Trim the wardrobe, sure, but the truth still clings:
We keep buying costumes ’cause we’re scared of skin.

prompt:
Resume's tight like jazz hands in a panic,
Ten tabs open, spiraling manic.
Refreshed LinkedIn like it’s my side hustle,
Still getting ghosted harder than a midlife muscle.

Rebranded burnout as a 'goal,' 
Still drowning in a spreadsheet hole
I networked so hard I sprained my pride
Sent 84 emails, got one "Please unsubscribe".

[Pre-Chorus Melodramatic Belt, arms to the heavens]
Refreshed LinkedIn like it’s my part-time gig,
Still ghosted harder than a burnt-out vape rig.
I’m a master of pivot, a guru of grit
But my inbox is just rejection... or spam shit 

I’m a suburban standout, khaki-clad dropout,
Gold medal in waiting, burnout in a blackout.
I’m a suburban standout, recliner-bound prophet,
Dreams on layaway, hope in the closet.

CEO of Plan B through Z,
President of “Why Won’t They Hire Me?”
Yeah, I’m a standout - outstandingly broke,
Fluent in sarcasm, spreadsheets, and smoke

Meal-prep dreams, snack on shame,
Got no unemployment, just bills in my name.
Used to lead teams with passion and vision,
Now I barter memes for dopamine hits, no commission.

“For Hire” taped to my bougainvillea,
My business cards printed at IKEA.
Therapist says, “Just try manifesting,”
But I’m stress-snacking through late-stage resting.

But hey, I’ve got vision.
And time.
And forty-seven versions of the same damn cover letter.
Hire me. Or don’t.
I’ll still be out here, standing out

Tried monetizing hobbies, failed with flair,
Even applied to jobs that weren’t really there.
That “interview” link sent me to a shed
Now I bring pepper spray just to job hunt without ending up dead.
Ghosted by HR, scammed by the rest
It's a Craigslist jungle in a LinkedIn vest.

Tried selling feet pics...too niche.
Tried a food blog...ate the niche.
Even launched a podcast: Just Me Crying,
But shockingly, still not monetizing.

Scrolled job boards, perks looked fine,
Clicked “Apply,” next thing? True crime.
Said “on-site interview”, what a twist
I mapped my escape, with a self-defense list.

I’m a suburban standout, burnout incarnate,
CEO of Plan Z, unpaid and snark laced.
Dodging scams in a LinkedIn vest,
Where “hiring now” means “hope for the best.”

But hey, I’ve got vision.
And work ethic
And a 9-millimeter in my tote just to check the job market.
Hire me. Or don’t.
But if your office is in a van with no windows
and “competitive pay” is spray-painted on the side
just know:
I come strapped…
with experience.

Learning not to reach.

That fit the golden rule.

Or dim the harder light.

And waits behind my teeth.

Beside a curtain dry.

Then swallow back inside.

The room is mostly clean.
But every day the floorboards shift
Where something might have been.

It’s subtraction.

And not getting up at all.

Turns out sanity’s the rarest art.

DSM-seasoned, socially stressed, chemically still.

Then lock us all in the same damn ward.

Maybe it’s baked in the way we’re fed.

That’s not pathology, that’s a void.

To a world that’s quietly hostile and messy.

Hands up if you’re barely functioning.
Hands up if the goalposts moved again
While they asked why you look so tense.

If surviving this takes meds, jokes, rage, and art,
Then hell yes, I’ve got the chart.
Yeah, we are all easily qualified as mentally ill
So stop asking what’s wrong with us
And start asking what this world did.

Call me unstable.
I call it awake.
If sanity means pretending this is fine
I’ll take my chances with the diagnosis.

I wrote a comment at 3 A.M.,
Sharp as a tack, a digital gem.
Posted it once, refreshed the page…
Zero likes, my tiny stage.

A miniseries, too,

By the endless tide.
